LESSON: PUBLIC PRESENTATION

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.5: Public Presentation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Public Presentation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we travel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify non-verbal cues for effective communication
2. apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation
3. appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PUBLIC PRESENTATION
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Public Presentation helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PUBLIC PRESENTATION
Study Public Presentation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify non-verbal cues for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify non-verbal cues for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify non-verbal cues for effective communication.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Public Presentation” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify non-verbal cues for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Public Presentation.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Public Presentation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Public Presentation” in your own words using one local example. (skill: identify non-verbal cues for effective communication)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Public Presentation. (skill: apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation)

Example 3: Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson. (skill: appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Public Presentation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify non-verbal cues for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate audience awareness in public presentation for lifelong learning.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Public Presentation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Public Presentation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Public Presentation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we travel?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Public Presentation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify non-verbal cues for effective communication.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate non- verbal cues in an oral presentation.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
